# lock-closures roadmap

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Closure chance vs upstream gauge level
      Objective: Show how the chance that one lock closes moves with its upstream river-gauge level, on real closure records and real gauge readings.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing built; real closure records and upstream gauge readings, acquired within this stage
      Produces: specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md (the closure-vs-gauge result and the measured cost of the real run); a fitted closure-vs-gauge model that later stages may build on
      Exit: the findings file reports the closure chance across the observed range of upstream gauge levels for one lock on real data, and records the measured cost of the real run: data volume, load time and fit time
      Leaves out: traceability: suggested, see the approval question
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

> Stage N: COMPLETE (YYYY-MM-DD) — implemented by plan <id> (path). Its Handoff section names what <stages> consume.
> Next: resume the roadmap.

## Completion

When every committed stage is ticked and the Ranked list is empty or parked,
re-run the gap rubric over the Outcomes list above (O1–O4, plus any outcome
added at a resume), with evidence per verdict: implementing stage and plan,
Deviation notes, and `specs/deferred_items.md` entries. Each unmet outcome
exits as a new stage or as a conscious deferral with a written why. Ranked-list
items never promoted have parked. Retire to `specs/completed/` only after
this review.

---

I've written `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md`. It holds one research track with your ranking O1 → O2 → O3 → O4.

- **Committed stage.** Only the core stage, Stage 1, is committed. It delivers O1 for one lock on real closure records and gauge readings. Its findings file records the result and the measured cost of the real run.
- **Ranked list.** O2, O3 and O4 wait in the Ranked list in your order. After Stage 1 has run on real data, the next resume reports what it found and what it cost, then asks you to re-rank the list.
- **Order.** The order follows your ranking. It also follows the dependencies:
  - O2's outlook reuses O1's model.
  - O3's cost is stated as a multiple of Stage 1's data.
  - O4 depends on nothing, but ranks last by your choice.

**One question:** Do you approve this partition?

In the same answer, please say whether you want **traceability** added to the track. Traceability means each closure estimate names the gauge readings it came from. The project will need it because the trust's board will ask which gauge readings each closure estimate came from. If you approve it, it becomes **O5: every closure estimate traces to the specific gauge readings it was computed from**, and it joins the Ranked list wherever you rank it among O2–O5. If you decline, Stage 1's `Leaves out` will record that.

Once you answer, I'll update the file, commit it on `main`, and give you the "Next:" line for Stage 1. Stage 1 starts in a fresh session with brainstorming.
